# Narrow nature

A daily puzzle that asks you to read a community instead of one organism. Six species were all recorded at one real iNaturalist place in one month. They're revealed the most widespread first: the first line gets you to the right part of the world, each one after it is more local, and the last one often names the valley. You drop a pin on a world map, pick a month, and score on distance, month and how few species you needed. Today's list is the same round for everyone; More lists deals up to ten more a day per browser from a separate set of places. It sits first in Things to try because it's the one people come back to. It was built after Truman turned down a rarity game as "the same idea as kriliion" and pointed at iNatGuessr as the bar: "inatguesser was unique and good" (2026-10-08).

The long version, including every accuracy rule, is [docs/hobbies.md](../../../docs/hobbies.md#reference-implementation-narrow-nature-daily-puzzle). Since 2026-11-24 the page is its own screen with its own look, like the title screen: a pixel world map, Jersey type, navy panels and keys that press, with no site header or footer (`section="game"` in BaseLayout). [hobby-pages](../hobby-pages/SKILL.md) still covers the card, the opening scene and the data, and [site-motion](../site-motion/SKILL.md) covers rapid clicks and reduced motion, but the site's ink-and-paper look and its motion timings don't apply inside the game.

## Truman's rules for the puzzle

- **Completely accurate, so experts can play it**: "it has to be completely accurate and also images. that way i can give it to experts and hobbyists who want to play" (2026-10-09). Every clue is a research-grade record from that place and month, with at least two local records.
- **Animals over plants.** "slightly more animal focused" (2026-10-09). Plants are dead-end clues for almost everyone.
- **Narrow from the first species.** "it's basically impossible to narrow down from first 4 animals. I would suggest making it more narrow from the start, because otherwise people have no chance" (2026-11-24). The opener gets you to a continent or a big part of one, each line after it is more local, and each card says how far from the place half its sightings are, so the board shows how much it narrows.
- **The premise comes first, in one line, and the how-to is pictures.** "everyone who has tried this is so confused the premise of the game" (2026-10-12) made the premise and four steps the biggest thing on the page. That became "the wall of text" (2026-11-24): "look at games like krillion, it's almost all graphic". The title panel now carries one rules line ("6 species · 1 place · 1 month · each one narrows the map"), and How to play is three small looping pictures with one short paragraph. Show a rule before writing it, and keep words off the map.
- **The map has to work on a phone**: zoom to see how close you were, more detail than flat continents, state and country borders (2026-10-12).
- **A phone's game fits what the browser leaves, with Lock it in on screen** (2026-11-24): a small title, a big map and nothing hidden. Safari and Brave leave an iPhone 14 about 390x664 of its 390x844, so size and test for that, in WebKit (ship-and-ci). The map stays the whole world, 1.6:1 at most and 2:1 at least, and the cards take the rest.
- **Photographer names stay off the board.** Credits go in a closed footnote, because a name can give the place away (2026-10-13).
- **More lists is capped at ten a day**, so places don't repeat and it doesn't cost much (2026-10-12).
- **Every fact on the full list follows site-copy Species facts: one sentence, 12 to 25 words.** A species with no fact shows no fact line. day-list.test.ts fails on an empty or '...' fact (2026-11-15). An empty one passes only when day-list-facts.json says why: Wikipedia has nothing on that species but taxonomy.
- **The share text names the list number and ends with the URL** (2026-11-15): "Narrow nature list 25, November 15", the squares, the numbers, then trumanbrown.com/hobbies/narrow-nature. On a phone the button says "Share result" and opens the share sheet. More lists has no share.
- **Nothing over the map covers the pin, the line or the answer** (2026-11-15, for the old verdict stamp on a phone). The verdict banner and the postcard are fixed panels, and the camera frames the answer in the room they leave (`room()`).
- **Hold the place name until the map has said where** (2026-11-15). The name, the verdict and the postcard wait until the finder box has locked on, so the map tells you first.
- **Feedback lands by what it's about, not in the middle of the screen**: the "-X points" stamp "slamming first like a stamp and slowly drifting down and away" (2026-10-14), on the top-right corner of the clue photo it bought: "its fine on the photo since the photo is large and this is small and in top right" (2026-10-25). Since mock D it's an arcade pop off that corner of the card, rising and fading in whole pixels, while the score top right ticks down.
- **Every species shows on the map** (2026-11-24, mock D): its ring round the pin is how far from the place half its sightings are, in a colour from its own photo, so the narrowing is something you see before it's a number you read.

## Add places or rebuild the rounds

1. Vet candidates: `node scripts/resolve-day-list-places.mjs` (add `--extra` for More lists). It resolves each to an iNaturalist place id and reports how much data it has, its busiest month and the size of its boundary.
2. Paste the keepers into `PLACES` or `EXTRA_PLACES` in `scripts/build-day-list.mjs`.
3. Build: `npm run build:day-list` (the daily set) or `npm run build:day-list -- --extra`. About an hour per set: it throttles to roughly one request a second, retries with a widening pause, and refuses to write a set with fewer than ten rounds. The reach counts are cached in `.cache/day-list/` for a week, so a rerun after retuning the bands only pays for photos and labels. The log prints each round's six reaches in km, and notes rounds that open narrow.
4. Write the facts. The build ends with the species that have no entry in `day-list-facts.json`; until they get one they carry the first sentence of their Wikipedia summary that isn't taxonomy, or nothing if it runs over 25 words, and `npm test` fails. Write each from its Wikipedia article to site-copy's Species facts (one sentence, 12 to 25 words, the hook first, no taxonomy), check it against the article, then run `npm run build:day-list -- --facts [--extra]`. That changes only facts and links, needs no network for written ones, and is safe any time.
5. Rebuild the daily set near midnight. Today's round is `todayNumber() % ROUNDS.length` by the visitor's local date, so adding or removing daily rounds changes everyone's "today", including people partway through. A daily place marked `hold: true` is skipped for that reason (four since 2026-11-24); a build that only changes species in the same places keeps everyone's today.
6. `npm run build:day-list -- --retag [--extra]` relabels native, introduced and endemic without changing any species (about ten minutes for both sets), and is safe any time.
7. Run `npx vitest run src/lib/hobbies/day-list.test.ts`. It reads the built data: the real sets must never share a place, every round needs six species and a boundary, there must be enough extras for a week, and every fact must match `day-list-facts.json` and pass the Species facts rule.
8. Record any fact check in the docs, as the October and November 2026 ones were.

## Map data

- Relief: `npm run build:day-list-relief`, and bump `VERSION` (`"v1"`) in the script whenever the tiles change, because `/day-list/relief/*` is served immutable. Static Web Apps allows 15,000 files per deploy, and the tiles are about 2,900 of them. They stay same-origin because the map reads their pixels to recolour them.
- Borders: `npm run build:day-list-borders`. It deletes files it no longer makes, so restart `npm run dev` if it was running.
- Both download Natural Earth into `.cache/` once.

## Hard-won lessons

1. **Plants made dead-end clues**: 9 of 21 giveaway lines were plants. Animals now sort first in every band, a round allows at most two botanical clues, and the last band is animals only. Plants went from 31% of clues to 1% (`bb02074`).
2. **Labels need a majority, not one listing.** A user-made iNaturalist place tagged Mallards as introduced across six rounds, and Grey Wagtail was called endemic on Madeira. A label now follows the majority of the place's own flagged records, and "endemic" needs at least half of the species' records worldwide flagged endemic (`3bf8d22`).
3. **Record counts aren't range.** Clues were ordered by worldwide records, and a round needed an opener with at least 120,000 of them so it wouldn't start half-solved. A count says how often a species is recorded, not where, so rounds opened on four birds found across a hemisphere (Hokkaido: Mallard, Common merganser, Reed bunting, Pine grosbeak), five African rounds all had Common hoopoe and Common warthog, and Domestic horse and Domestic cat were clues. Truman: "basically impossible to narrow down from first 4 animals" (2026-11-24). The builder now measures each candidate's reach, the distance from the place holding half its research-grade records (17 rings, one `species_counts` call each, cached a week in `.cache/day-list/`), and takes one clue per band of reach: 1,500 km and up, 900, 500, 250, 100, under 100. Species with 80% of their records within 4,500 km go first. That test was 3,200 km at first, and Olympic, in a corner of its continent, failed every American species and opened on the Mallard again. Wikipedia links from iNaturalist arrive with raw spaces and have to be normalized (`283694e`).
4. **A photographer's name gave the place away** (Cyrillic on a Białowieża photo). Credits moved to a closed footnote (`887f540`).
5. **On a phone the map was "a strip of flat continents with no way in".** It got zoom to 64x, double-tap, Ctrl or Cmd plus scroll (plain scroll scrolled the page and showed a hint), relief tiles and a scale bar (`3bf8d22`). The pin drops only on a click that didn't move, so a scroll that starts on the map can't drop one (`ba360e4`). The full-screen game has no page to scroll, so plain scroll zooms there (`wheelZoom`), and the rings took over from the scale bar.
6. **Borders from Natural Earth needed work**: its zoom limits left Mexico blank beside a fully drawn US, and state lines ran across bays such as the Chesapeake. Each country's zoom now comes from its states' sizes, and lines that cross water are dropped (`27fdb80`).
7. **The reveal reads better in beats.** The panel used to print the verdict and the place the moment you locked in, so 700 ms later it had already said "Table Mountain" while the map was still moving. Since mock D the beats are: the camera frames pin and place, the bullseye slides to the place with the dotted line behind it, the boundary inks in, the finder box locks on and prints the coordinates, and only then the name, the verdict banner, the score and the postcard. Under reduced motion, or for a finished round restored on load, it all shows at once.
8. **The rename went in two commits**, title and copy first (`dfca9e4`), then the URL with 301s from the old paths (`a9c0572`). The code kept the old name on purpose.
9. **The full list printed Wikipedia as it came**: taxonomy ("a member of the duck, goose, and swan family Anatidae"), facts cut at "subspecies of P." and lines of nothing but "...". In the daily set 10 of 234 facts were empty or "..." and 136 ran over 25 words, because the builder kept the first 230 characters of each summary. The page now shows one sentence and hides a stub (`a5f11e7`). Every fact is written by hand in `day-list-facts.json`, checked against its article, and the test holds the data to the Species facts rule. Eleven species have only taxonomy on Wikipedia and show no fact rather than an invented one. The first `--facts` run blanked every Wikipedia link it had no taxon to read from, so `--facts` now keeps a clue's link unless the facts file sets one, and a test checks the links.
10. **The verdict stamp covered the pin on a phone.** It always sat top left, and on a 390 by 195 map a stamp about 190 by 55 px covered a third of it, pin and line included. `placeVerdict` then hunted for the clearest corner before the camera moved, and four rounds still had nowhere to go. Mock D (2026-11-24) dropped the stamp: on a phone the postcard docks at the foot and the map takes the space between it and the verdict banner, keeping its 1.6:1 shape and running past the screen's sides (`shownWidth`), with a shorter map for an answer too wide for the middle to hold. Lay the panels out first, then frame the answer in the room they leave.
11. **The full-screen phone layout hid Lock it in on real iPhones** (2026-11-24). It was checked in Chromium at 390x844, the whole screen, but Safari and Brave leave about 390x664, and with html and body set to `overflow: hidden` the months and Lock it in sat below the screen with no way to scroll to them. The 150px title and two rows of 112 to 152px cards had also squeezed the map to 390x196. Laptops between 1,010 and 1,240px wide had the months covering the last cards, because the short-screen rule fixed cards at 104px. The phone now sizes itself from the screen (`layout`): a two-row title, the whole world at 1.6:1, photo-only cards with a strip naming the picked one, and the months as a keypad beside Lock it in, scrolling only as a last resort. Cards on bigger screens are sized by the room beside the months. Before pushing a layout change, play a round in WebKit with Playwright's iPhone presets (iPhone 14, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 14 Pro Max, iPhone SE) and sweep laptop widths from 760 to 1,920 for overlaps.

## Gotchas

- Keep the `day-list-*` localStorage keys, the `dayList` block and the `data-daylist-*` hooks. Saved progress depends on them.
- `day-list.test.ts` and `day-list-borders.test.ts` read the built data, so a bad rebuild fails `npm test`.
- Everything built at runtime is styled through the namespaced global style block; scoped styles don't reach it.
- The share string uses emoji squares because it goes to the clipboard or the share sheet; on-page copy never uses emoji. It's the one exception in site-copy's "Do not write".
- `room()` reads the panels' sizes from the page, so a CSS change to the score, the zoom keys or the postcard changes where the answer is framed. Check a few rounds at 390x844 and 1440x900 after one.
- Every copy of a photo loads with `crossorigin="anonymous"` (cards, postcard, full list, the preload in `photo()`). The ring colours and tokens read the photo's pixels, and iNaturalist's bucket varies on `Origin`, so one copy cached without CORS can stop a canvas reading it. `static.inaturalist.org` sends no CORS header at all, so the builder takes photos only from the open-data bucket and a test checks both sets.
- The map draws in `ENCODED` colours (plain grey relief, pure blue borders, no graticule) and `day-list-pixel.ts` repaints them, so a change to the map's own drawing has to keep those colours apart.
- The page has no theme toggle (no header). It follows `html.dark`, set from the visitor's choice elsewhere on the site or their device.
- Puzzle data ships as JSON and photos load from the iNaturalist CDNs, so playing costs nothing per visit and works if the API is down. Keep it that way.

Add new verdicts and lessons here, dated, in the commit that acts on them.
